results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system, as recorded in VFB. VFB describes the mushroom body as divided into: the calyx, which is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, which is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records of neurons with some part in mushroom body, [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") records of parts of mushroom body, and [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") records of subclasses of mushroom body. For further information, you can explore the available images of mushroom body, or examine the neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body, among other options.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response:
The adult Drosophila brain contains multiple types of Kenyon cells, including gamma Kenyon cells. VFB records show that there are several types of Kenyon cells, such as KCab-c(i), KCab-c, KCg-m, Kenyon cell of main calyx, and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes including alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells. The connectome data indicates that gamma Kenyon cells can be further classified into subclasses. VFB holds [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100247,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of gamma Kenyon cell") records of subclasses of gamma Kenyon cells, including [larval [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain")](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049827 "Open larval gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-s](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049830 "Open KCg-s in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-s4](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049832 "Open KCg-s4 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-t](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049833 "Open KCg-t in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-d](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110932 "Open KCg-d in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCg-m, KCg-s1, KCg-s2, KCg, and KCg-s3. 

VFB has annotated data on gamma Kenyon cells, including images, splits targeting gamma Kenyon cells, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, downstream connectivity classes, and upstream connectivity classes. The exact number of records for each of these can be found by running the respective queries.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior and has a unique anatomy and connectivity. According to VFB, it has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and its large descending axon is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, the giant fiber neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The neuron enters the ventral nerve cord near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally and ends abruptly without branching. In the mesothoracic neuromere, it forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge and at the axonal lateral bend. 

VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron is a primary neuron. Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron include P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD}, P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, and P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD}. Relevant publications include Phelan et al., 1996, King and Wyman, 1980, Stürner et al., 2025, Dorkenwald et al., 2024, Namiki et al., 2018, Thomas and Wyman, 1984, Koto et al., 1981, Power, 1948, Ito et al., 2014, Kamikouchi et al., 2009, Kennedy and Broadie, 2018, Allen et al., 1998, Bacon and Strausfeld, 1986, Matsuo et al., 2016, and Kim et al., 2020.

VFB holds [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the giant fiber neuron, as well as data on [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting it, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") cases of transgene expression in it, [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes, and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes. The connectome data indicates that the giant fiber neuron has specific downstream and upstream connectivity, which can be explored further through VFB.
